links.note: Where the Buddha was born - northern India. Part of the princely life he later left, which is 24227.
When he was sent for schooling - at twelve. The sheltered early life before the renunciation.
Sent away for schooling at twelve - the palace upbringing of 24227.
His age at renouncing the princely life - twenty-five. 24227 is that renunciation.
Married to a princess at sixteen - the sheltered life he afterwards gave up.
About ten years of royal married life - the period before he left the palace.
Sakyamuni as a name of Gautama Buddha - the prince who renounced his palace.
His birth year, 563 BC - a fact of the princely life described in 24227.
His death in 483 BC - part of the biographical frame around the renunciation.
Why Prince Siddhartha left the palace and became a beggar - the sickness, old age and death he saw. 24227 names exactly these.
What Siddhartha saw when out hunting and the impression it made - the sick man, the old man, the funeral procession, which drove the renunciation.
How he began life and where he was sent at twelve - the palace upbringing he later renounced.
The fate of mortals - inevitable death for all. 24233 states that none escapes it.
Mortals always in danger of death - 24233's point exactly.
What the Buddha asked the grieving woman for - a handful of seed from a house untouched by death. That condition is 24231.
How the Buddha answered Kisa Gotami's request and what that shows of his teaching - the mustard-seed task rather than a direct lesson.
What the Buddha told her about life - that sorrow is universal and must be accepted. That is 24226.
What the Buddha says about the world - afflicted with death and decay, so the wise do not grieve. The central message.
How Kisa felt when she could find no such seed - the moment her understanding turns, which is 24232.
What she asks for on the second round of houses and why she cannot get it - no house is untouched by death. 24232's realisation.
She asked the villagers whether they had lost a loved one - the question that brings the realisation.
Kisa comparing human life to the city lights flickering and going out - the image in which her realisation is expressed.
Where the Buddha sat - under a fig tree. 24228 is that tree and the seven days.
Where and when Siddhartha became the Buddha - under the fig tree after seven days.
Those who do not grieve are wise - 24234 is the futility of lamenting.
'The wise do not grieve, knowing the terms of the world' - the futility of lamentation in 24234.
What he named the tree - the Bodhi Tree. 24229 is that renaming.
Sketch of Gautama Buddha as the enlightened personality who renamed the tree and began to teach - 24229's subject.
Kisa Gotami tired and devoid of hope - the mother's grief as she carries her son from house to house.
Discussion prompt on thinking of oneself as unique or as one among billions - one of the guided questions before the text, which is 24237.
Glossing 'blessed' as 'lucky' - the dictionary work 24236 asks for.
